sections.heading: Introduction: Why Wavelength Calibration Matters
paragraphs: Wavelength calibration is a critical step in maintaining the accuracy, precision, and reliability of a UV-Vis or NIR spectrometer. Without periodic calibration, even top-grade instruments can drift, causing errors in spectral measurements. At ITC India, we use traceable standards and rigorous ISO/IEC 17025 compliant procedures to ensure your instruments perform as intended.

sections.heading: 1. Spectrometer
bullets: UV-Vis double beam spectrophotometer
NIR spectrometer (for broader range calibration)

sections.heading: 2. Calibration Standards & Tools
paragraphs: 📸 Visual Note: Calibration setup includes a stable optical bench, cuvette holder, computer interface, and temperature-controlled sample environment.
bullets: Mercury-Argon Lamp: For accurate line emission (Ocean Insight)
Holmium Oxide Filters: Used to verify peak positions (NIST Reference Material)
Potassium Dichromate Solution: For absorbance validation
Toluene in Hexane: For assessing instrument resolution
Spectral Calibration Software: Polynomial fitting and peak matching

sections.heading: ➤ Step 1: Lamp-Based Calibration (Emission Line Matching)
paragraphs: λ(p) = I + C₁p + C₂p² + C₃p³ Where λ(p) is the calibrated wavelength at pixel p.
bullets: The mercury-argon lamp is activated and aligned with the sample port.
Sharp emission peaks at known wavelengths (e.g., 253.65 nm, 365.02 nm) are recorded.
A third-order polynomial is used to map pixel data to wavelength.

sections.heading: ➤ Step 2: Absorbance Calibration
paragraphs: 🔗 Read more about UV-Vis absorbance standards
bullets: Prepare a 60 mg potassium dichromate solution in 0.005M sulfuric acid.
Measure absorbance at 235 nm, 257 nm, 313 nm, and 350 nm.
Compare results with the European Pharmacopeia accepted ranges:235 nm: 122.9 – 126.2

sections.heading: ➤ Step 3: Resolution Check
bullets: Use toluene in hexane.
Scan from 260 nm to 270 nm.
Verify peak-to-valley ratio (A269/A266) is ≥ 1.5.

sections.heading: 📊 Case Study: Calibration of a Dual-Beam UV-Vis Spectrometer
paragraphs: Client: Pharmaceutical Testing Laboratory Instrument: Shimadzu UV-1800 Problem: Wavelength drift over time causing ±2 nm deviation

sections.heading: Calibration Action Taken:
bullets: Pre-calibration error: Emission peak at 365 nm was recorded at 367.1 nm
After recalibration using Hg-Ar lamp and holmium oxide filter, error reduced to ±0.02 nm
Resolution confirmed using toluene standard

sections.heading: Outcome:
bullets: Instrument passed all required tolerances for GLP compliance
Issued ISO 17025-compliant calibration certificate
Client’s FDA inspection cleared without remarks
